meta.label: Repair and tailoring
meta.attribution: Every option here is a way to get a worn or damaged garment mended, altered or reproofed instead of replaced. Scores are judgments made from each provider's own published terms, read in September 2026, meaning a price list, a help page or a policy. They are not audited outcomes and no provider was asked to check them. Most brand programmes repair only that brand's own clothes, so the practical choice depends on what is in the wardrobe. Repair Cafés and mending at home are the routes here that do not depend on the label, and SOJO in the UK lists its services by kind of damage rather than by label. A cost score rewards free or low published prices. An ease score rewards walk-in or postal access, short stated waits and few exclusions. The transparency score reflects how much of the price, the waiting time and the exclusions the provider publishes. Where a provider publishes no price or no waiting time, that cell is left empty rather than estimated. A local independent tailor is the obvious comparison and is left unscored, because independent tailors publish no shared price list, and Timpson in the UK could not be scored because its pages refused automated reading. Prices are in each provider's own currency (pounds for the UK ones, dollars for the US ones) and change without much notice, so check the linked page. Reviewed 2026-09. Suggest changes via Contribute.

criteria.label: Low cost to the customer, free or a published low price
Easy to get done: walk-in or post, short wait, few exclusions (ease of use, not disability access)
Publishes its prices, waiting time and what it will not repair

products.name: Nudie Jeans Repair Shops
products.description: Free repairs on Nudie Jeans, done at the brand's own repair shops and partner stores, including hemming and zip exchanges.

economical.note: Nudie Jeans' repair help page says jeans can be repaired for free at any Nudie Jeans Repair Store or Repair Partner, as many times as wanted, no matter when or where they were bought. It also says zip exchanges are free.

accessibility.note: The same help page says the service is exclusive to Nudie Jeans, accepts only freshly washed jeans, and has no send-in option, because the brand says shipping single pieces would harm the environment. Repairs happen in a Repair Store or at a Repair Partner.

transparency.note: The help page states the price (free), the hand-in condition (freshly washed) and the scope, but gives no waiting time. It says each shop's handling time depends on workload and tells customers to ask their local shop.

products.name: RE.UNIQLO Studio
products.description: In-store repair, remake and tailoring service for Uniqlo clothes, priced from a published menu.

economical.note: Uniqlo's UK RE.UNIQLO Studio price list gives an invisible hole repair from 5 pounds, bobble removal at 4 pounds, button replacement at 4 pounds per item, a full zip replacement at 15 pounds and a shortened hem at 10 pounds. The cheapest listed item on the menu is 3 pounds.

accessibility.note: The price list states in two places that all stated prices apply to Uniqlo items only. It does not say which stores have a studio or how long a repair takes.

transparency.note: The menu is a full published list across repair, remake and tailoring, with 'from' marked on variable items. It gives no waiting time.

products.name: Levi's Tailor Shop
products.description: In-store alterations, repairs and customisation counters inside Levi's stores.

economical.note: Levi's help page on Red Tab member benefits says repair pricing starts at $5.00 and varies with the repair. Repairs are free for manufacturing defects covered by the quality guarantee and for broken belt loops, buttons, rivets and the Two Horse back patch. The repair section sits under Red Tab member benefits, and the page does not say whether non-members can use it.

accessibility.note: The same page gives typical waits of same day for simple repairs, 2 to 6 business days for structural repairs, 1 to 2 weeks for waist adjustments and paneling, and 3 to 4 weeks for custom tailoring and upcycling. It says Tailor Shops in the US and Canada do not do zipper repairs.

transparency.note: The UK Tailor Shop page lists services with prices, for example sundries from 3 to 15 pounds, alterations from 10 to 80 pounds and paneling from 40 to 70 pounds. Distressing and repairing are listed as price based on request, and members get 50 per cent off.

products.name: Arc'teryx ReBIRD Repair
products.description: Warranty and paid repair of Arc'teryx outerwear, through service centres, brand stores or mail-in.

economical.note: Arc'teryx's product service page says minor repairs such as small tears and defective buckles, cord locks or zipper pulls can be done in store or at home for free. Complex repairs from wear and tear, accidents or misuse get a free evaluation and a quote that the owner approves before any fee-based work starts.

accessibility.note: The page says a repair claim can start at a ReBIRD brand store, online or at home, the owner ships the product in and Arc'teryx pays the return shipping. Gear not bought from authorized retailers, and items such as base layers, socks, harnesses and hydration reservoirs, are not eligible.

transparency.note: The page explains the two repair categories, the exclusions and who pays shipping, and says the assessment time is posted on the request form. It publishes no price list and gives a repair time estimate only after assessment.

products.name: Filson Repairs
products.description: Mail-in repair of Filson goods, free under the lifetime warranty and paid otherwise.

economical.note: Filson's repairs page says there is no charge for warranty repairs. If damage is repairable but not covered by warranty, the owner may have it repaired at their own expense after a Repair Representative reviews the options. No price list is given.

accessibility.note: The page asks customers to allow 6 to 8 weeks for repairs, and items are sent to Filson. It lists boots, gloves, hats, down-insulated goods, dry bags and technical synthetics as items it cannot repair.

transparency.note: The page states the waiting time, the warranty exclusions and what happens if an item cannot be repaired, including a returned letter for out-of-warranty items. It publishes no prices.

products.name: Barbour Re-wax and Repair
products.description: Paid re-waxing, repair and alteration of Barbour jackets, ordered from an itemised online menu.

economical.note: Barbour's UK page prices a re-wax at 35 pounds and a clean and re-wax at 50 pounds. Repairs are itemised, for example re-stitching a seam 10 pounds, a small patch 17 pounds, a large patch 35 pounds, a new zip 30 pounds and shortening sleeves 35 pounds.

transparency.note: The same page lists each service and its price by part of the jacket, covering front, sleeves, back, collar, lining and length alterations. It states no turnaround time.

products.name: Rab Service Centre
products.description: Priced repairs of Rab waterproof and insulated clothing at the brand's UK service centre.

economical.note: Rab's waterproof repairs page lists a zip slider replacement at 10 pounds, patch and cuff tab repairs at 15 pounds, a large patch at 25 pounds, a shell wash at 15 pounds and a full shell zip replacement at 35 pounds.

accessibility.note: The page gives the current turnaround as about 2 weeks from receipt of the item and asks customers to send their Rab waterproof gear in. It describes repairs for Rab waterproof items.

transparency.note: The page publishes a price for each repair type and a current turnaround time.

products.name: Fjällräven repair
products.description: Repairs of Fjällräven gear at flagship stores or by mail-in approved through the warranty team.

accessibility.note: Fjällräven's North America support page says that only flagship stores can process repairs at present, with no appointment needed if the item is clean, listing New York, Seattle, Toronto and Vancouver. Elsewhere, customers submit a request so the warranty team can approve a mail-in repair at a repair hub.

transparency.note: A Fjällräven North America support page says the repair process can take up to 4 to 6 weeks in peak season. The two support pages read give no repair prices.

products.name: VAUDE Reparaturservice
products.description: Repair service for VAUDE products through an online portal and dealers, described on a German-language page.

accessibility.note: VAUDE's German repair page says it offers repairs for all its products through an online portal and says the process normally takes 14 working days plus transport. Bike bags, sleeping mats and shoes cannot be sent through the portal and are handled separately, and warranty cases can be lodged at a dealer.

transparency.note: The page says the repair team checks whether a repair is possible and whether it is a warranty case, then emails the result and any cost, with a payment link if costs arise. It publishes no price list.

products.name: Mammut Repair and Care
products.description: Postal repair of Mammut jackets, pants, sleeping bags, gloves and shoes, with a published price list in euros.

economical.note: Mammut's help centre publishes a repair price list in euros, excluding VAT and shipping, with a zipper puller replacement at 0 euros, a seam stitch repair at 10 euros, patching a hole or tear at 25 euros, shortening sleeves at 45 euros and replacing a pocket zip at 50 to 70 euros. It also lists covering a down baffle with fabric at 45 euros.

accessibility.note: Mammut's request page says a customer fills in a contact form with proof of purchase and a photo of the damage, then posts the item once Mammut confirms the request. Only clean products can be repaired, and repairs can take up to about 5 weeks in the October to April high season.

transparency.note: Mammut publishes a price list by product type and says the customer receives a cost estimate if the repair would exceed the maximum amount entered on the form. It also gives a high-season waiting time and says an alternative is offered if a repair is not possible.

products.name: SOJO
products.description: A UK postal repair and alterations service with Royal Mail collection and a Selfridges concession in London.

economical.note: SOJO's pricing table lists starting prices such as 5 pounds for a button or popper, 20 for a rip or trouser shortening, 35 for a zip replacement, 40 for shortening a suit jacket and 60 for an outerwear panel replacement. It says final prices vary with material, damage location and finish.

accessibility.note: SOJO says customers post the item or have Royal Mail collect it, and that standard turnaround is 7 days from arrival at the studio, or 3 days with express, excluding delivery. The page lists services by kind of damage rather than by brand, and there is an in-person concession at Selfridges London.

transparency.note: SOJO publishes a price table, both turnaround times and a note that complex repairs needing custom materials take longer. It gives an exact quote through a booking flow before any work.

products.name: Repair Cafés
products.description: Volunteer-run community repair events where visitors mend their own clothes and other items with help and tools provided.

economical.note: The Repair Café Foundation's about page describes Repair Cafés as free meeting places where volunteers with repair skills help with repairs.

accessibility.note: The same page says there are over 2,500 Repair Cafés worldwide and that tools and materials are on hand for repairs on clothes and other items. Visitors repair items together with volunteers.

products.name: Patagonia repair
products.description: Repair of Patagonia gear by mail or at a Patagonia store, with the Ironclad Guarantee covering defects.

accessibility.note: Patagonia's Worn Wear repairs page says its repair technicians can try to fix damaged gear that is mailed in or brought to a store, and that gear beyond repair is recycled. It also points to more than 100 care and repair guides made with iFixit.

transparency.note: The repairs page gives no price or waiting time. The Worn Wear FAQ quotes the Ironclad Guarantee, which says damage due to wear and tear will be repaired at a reasonable charge without saying what that charge is.

products.name: Mend it yourself with repair guides
products.description: Fixing seams, patches and zips at home from step-by-step guides, such as the ones iFixit publishes with Patagonia.

accessibility.note: iFixit's Patagonia care and repair page lists guide groups for seams and stitches, patches, zippers, notions and packs, plus a general sewing skills guide. The page does not say what the guides cost, and the work, tools and skill are the owner's.
